slot.brief: Object moved toward a concave mirror; use mirror formula with sign convention to find image position and magnification.

stem: A concave mirror has a focal length of $20$ cm. An object is placed at $50$ cm from the mirror. If the object is moved $20$ cm closer to the mirror, the distance of the image from the mirror will be

verdicts.working: After moving 20 cm closer, the object is 30 cm from the mirror. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v: 1/20 = 1/30 + 1/v, so v = 60 cm.

working:
Mirror formula $\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$. With $f = -20$ cm, new object distance $u = -30$ cm. $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{-20} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = -\dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{60}$. Hence $v = -60$ cm. Distance of image from mirror $= |v| = 60$ cm.

Independent check: After moving 20 cm closer, the object is 30 cm from the mirror. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v: 1/20 = 1/30 + 1/v, so v = 60 cm.
solution:
After moving $20$ cm closer, the object distance is $30$ cm. Using the mirror formula with Cartesian signs, $u=-30$ cm and $f=-20$ cm:
$$\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{u}=-\frac{1}{20}+\frac{1}{30}=-\frac{1}{60}$$
Thus $v=-60$ cm, so the image is $60$ cm from the mirror.
